title: Interpreting the Problem
text: The first step is to interpret the problem. < means "less than," so we know the valid domain is all numbers less than $$2.5$$.

title: Graphing the Solution
text: On a number line, shade to the left of $$2.5$$, and put a parentheses at $$2.5$$. The answer should look like the image attached to this hint.\n##figure3.gif##

figureAlts.figure3.gif: A number line from 0 to 3, with tick labels 0, 1, 2, 2.5, and 3. It is shaded from 2.5 to the left, with an arrow showing it continues forever to the left. A parenthesis at 2.5 shows that 2.5 is excluded.

title: Interval Notation: Parentheses and Brackets
text: In interval notation, parentheses show that the endpoint of the inequality is not included. For example, the expression "x>3" includes all numbers greater than $$3$$. Since $$3$$ is not included in the solution, the interval notation is $$(3,\infty)$$. Since $$\infty$$ represents "infinity" and is not an actual number, we always put a parenthesis next to $$\infty$$.

title: Example of Interval Notation
text: The attached image shows the inequality, number line, and interval notation of $$x>3$$.\n##figure4.gif##

figureAlts.figure4.gif: A number line from -5 to 5, labeled x is greater than 3. It is shaded from 3 to the right, with an arrow showing it continues forever. A parenthesis at 3 shows that 3 is excluded. Below it, the interval from 3 to infinity, excluding 3.
